title: action-2002-television
label: 'The Original' Jeff Garvin

won.source: The fed's own card (2003-01-27), submission finish (Hammer Jammer)

note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Garvin's loss of the belt is never shown. Two later matches corroborate KSZ holding it again by 2003-02-16 (the 2003-02-16 bout against 'The Original' Jeff Garvin, a non-title tournament bout where Garvin, having taken the belt off KSZ in the fray, sportingly HANDS IT BACK -- "Garvin held out the title to him?!... KSZ... took his belt"; and the 2003-02-24 bout against Invalid, KSZ entering "TV Title strapped over his shoulder"). The 2003-02-10 bout, KSZ vs Topex, dates the actual turnover in its own retrospective prose: "He had beaten Jeff Garvin on Whatever for it just a few days before, going the entire fifteen minutes and winning it back with a 450 Splash just seconds before the time limit expired." "Whatever" bookings in the window: Whatever 6 (2003-01-17) is already accounted for above (action-tv-001's defence); Whatever 7 (2003-02-07) is one of the fed's own 16 honest-absence shows (marked "Not located") -- so the match this quote describes almost certainly IS Whatever 7, but no card text survives to confirm the date to the day. Filed at won_precision 'circa' on the next reign (action-tv-003) rather than resolved here. No defence text survives for this reign.

Defended vs Topex (2003-02-10, submission -- Dragon Clutch, part of the 'King of Submission' tournament, not itself billed as a title defence in the match name but confirmed a defence by its own text quoted above), vs Angel Dawson (03-07, pinfall -- "KSZ via Pinfall"), vs Joey Malone (04-14, pinfall -- "KSZ via Pinfall"). Also seen holding the belt, non-title, on 2003-02-16 and 02-24 (vs Invalid, double DQ). No card for the night of this change survives in Action!'s own booking record; the date is the fed's own title history's.

note: Defended clean on Pressure Point 91 (2004-01-28, vs Mike "The Jobber" Rogers -- "Outcome: Atken via Pinfall; Retains A Title"). Pressure Point 92 (2004-04-07), the fed's own last show, leaves his status open twice ("the status of their Champion, Phil Atken still unclear"; "do you know if Phil Atken is returning?") and never narrates a loss. The fed's own record ends with its own last word 9 July 2004; the reign is filed open, to the record's end, not to an invented loss.

note: PRE-HISTORY, 2002-03-31 ('Resentment' special): another match missing from the title log, 'Bantam Championship: Matt Remicho vs. Areumna'derin Rahl,' a ladder match Remicho wins on-screen. But this predates the Bantam belt's real creation by over three months, and the show's own follow-up segment (billed 'B Championship?') has owner Reed Young announce beforehand that the title 'will still go on the line' despite the media's doubts, then AFTER Remicho wins, Young comes out and says 'it's way too soon to bring out the B Title... so I'm pulling it back' -- Remicho then lays Young out with the belt he never legitimately holds. No championship existed to change hands: this is a non-event, not a reign, and not a defence of anything (the real Bantam Championship is created by tournament four months later, at Joey Malone's win above). Filed here as a note on the title, not a reign row. Defended clean on 2002-07-24 (B & C Championship two-belt match, shared with Carnage -- see carnage-001's note), 08-14 (vs The Joker), 09-18 (vs Jeff Garvin).

title: action-2002-king-of-submission
label: Max Danger

won.source: Action Wrestling's own card Blood, Sweat, and Tears (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-blood-sweat-and-tears-2003-02-16.html): the ring announcer calls the King of Submissions Tournament Finals, the winner to receive “this three-foot tall trophy”, and the match closes “Outcome: Danger via Towel; Wins Submission Tournament.” The Action! Awards of 13 March 2003 (/promotions/action-2002/archive/action-2002-the-action-awards-2003-2003-03-13.html) has Danger recount the final and his 2003 King of Submission trophy stand at his table. His own card reads “2003 King of Submission” and Jeff Garvin's “Finalist in 'King of Submission' Tournament” (/promotions/action-2002/archive/max-danger-acw-bio.html; /promotions/action-2002/archive/jeff-garvin-bio.html).

how: Won the tournament final at Blood, Sweat, and Tears when Garvin's corner threw in the towel.
